errors.why: ཡེ་ཤེས is wisdom/gnosis (jñāna), not faith; the list item is 'what his wisdom is'.

errors.english: "May all merits, such as generosity, become concordant causes and may my generosity become inexhaustible."
errors.why: The purpose clause (so that all merits produce concordant results) is outside the dedication, and the dedication itself reads 'may the giving become distinguished and inexhaustible'; 'distinguished' is dropped and the purpose is put into the quoted wish.

note: Accurate commentary on the Buddhānusmṛti epithets apart from rendering ཡེ་ཤེས as 'faith' and a reshaped dedication formula.

errors.english: Once the sign of stability is not found
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'having found the sign of stability', parallel to the other families; the negation is invented.

fix.find: Once the sign of stability is not found
fix.replace: Once the sign of stability is found

note: The subtle-yoga and recitation sequence is followed closely, but one inserted negation inverts the instruction for the Jewel family.

errors.english: At that time, it is said that the wheel has the nature of time.
errors.why: འཁོར་ལོ་དུས་ here is most likely the Kālacakra (wheel of time) as a name/lemma ('having the nature of Kālacakra'), not 'the wheel has the nature of time'.

note: A technical death-sign computation passage rendered serviceably, with the corrupt 'ten' in the number series rightly read as thirty.

errors.english: will not be attained [note: if one remains attached to worldly appearances]
errors.why: The condition for not attaining siddhi is being devoid of the meditation on non-arising ('abandoning that'), not attachment to worldly appearances.

note: The sixteen emptinesses, four māras and generation/completion-stage purities are rendered faithfully; one closing note misstates the condition.

errors.english: Who are turning the wheel in various ways.
errors.why: The two lines 'May I too, by the power of intellect, enter their inexhaustible melodious speech' are not translated.

fix.find: Who are turning the wheel in various ways.
fix.replace:
Who are turning the wheel in various ways,
May I too, through the power of my intellect, enter
Their inexhaustible melodious speech.

note: A sound rendering of the Bhadracarī verses except for one dropped couplet at the top of the side.

errors.english: two initiations such as the water initiation are granted at the northern, southern, and eastern gates
errors.why: གཉིས་གཉིས is distributive: two initiations at EACH of the three gates (six, plus the permission at the west = the seven initiations named below).

fix.find: two initiations such as the water initiation are granted at the northern, southern, and eastern gates
fix.replace: two initiations each, beginning with the water initiation, are granted at the northern, southern, and eastern gates

errors.english: this refers to the purifications of the body and so forth; it is the different purification of the (dhatus) elements and (skandhas) aggregates
errors.why: ལས here is comparative: 'other' means other than the purities of body etc., namely the purities of the elements and aggregates.

errors.english: authorizing the student to practice a specific deity
errors.why: Unmarked explanatory addition not in the Tibetan, and misleading for the Kālacakra permission initiation.

note: The Kālacakra initiation sequence is broadly right, but the distributive count, the 'other than' comparison and an unmarked gloss need correction.
A careful 84000-style rendering of the sixteen forsakings and the emptiness-not-joined-to-emptiness commentary.

errors.english: though she was agitated by the haste of his departure
errors.why: It is the son, once sent off, who is flustered by haste (Skt. visṛṣṭas tvarākulaḥ), not the mother.

fix.find: though she was agitated by the haste of his departure
fix.replace: and, sent off, he went flustered by haste

errors.why: Sudharmā is the mother (the next sentences use 'she'/'his mother'), so it is her son.

note: The Tibetan verses of this bilingual jātaka page are followed well, with one subject switched and the pronoun of the queen confused.

errors.english: as it is from these that one must emerge from afflictive emotions
errors.why: The reason contrasts with the transcendent (emerging from afflictions): the worldly belongs to the three realms because it arises in/with the afflictions, not because one must emerge from them.

note: A faithful word-commentary on the tantric practices, with one muddled reason in the worldly/transcendent contrast.
A faithful rendering of the rain verses and Śakra's praise closing the Fish jātaka.
